blocking.section: Context and problem statement; Decision drivers; Decision outcome; Pros and cons of the options (Native Kafka wire-protocol proxying)
blocking.issue: The ADR says per-message routing is what P7 requires, and it rejects wire proxying as 'breaking P7'. P7 in the vision document maps a session to the request Phases and each message to onChunk. It does not give each message a Route. The owning document labels per-message routing through the request Phases a P7 exception and leaves it pending OQ-multi-protocol-18. Its option (b) is the P7-conforming shape: a session Route, with each message handled as onChunk. The ADR therefore contradicts the vision document and the owning document. It also rests its main rejection of option 7 on a misreading of P7. A wire proxy could conform to P7 by mapping a connection to the request Phases and record batches to onChunk. The real objections are the rewriting of metadata and coordinator responses, and that no per-message Route, Consumer or request-Phase Policy exists.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 19: "Each message stays inside the Route, Policy and Filter Chain model (P7)". Line 29: "- **One Filter Chain (P7)**: each message needs a Route; record batches seen by a wire proxy do not have one." Line 43: "and mediation keeps every message on a Route." Line 141: "its Phases see record batches with no per-message Route, breaking P7." Vision, Principles: "| P7 | Protocols are native | Every protocol maps onto the same `Route`, `Policy` and Filter Chain model through a documented Phase mapping: a session maps to the request Phases, each message to `onChunk`". Owning doc, Topic ingress: "Each message is a request on the Route whose `match.topic` matches, headers as headers and value as body, running the request Phases (a P7 exception: OQ-multi-protocol-18)." OQ-multi-protocol-18: "Should an ADR record the P7 exception for per-message routing ... (b) A session Route at CONNECT, PUBLISH as `onChunk`, conforming to P7".
blocking.fix: Rewrite the driver as: "- **Per-message governance (P7 exception, OQ-multi-protocol-18)**: each HTTP publish has a Route, and topic ingress and embedded PUBLISH run each message through the request Phases of a `match.topic` Route. The owning document records this as a P7 exception until OQ-multi-protocol-18 closes. A wire proxy sees record batches with no per-message Route or Consumer." In Context, replace "(P7)" with "(a P7 exception pending OQ-multi-protocol-18)". In the Chosen option sentence, write "mediation keeps every message on a Route (P7 exception, OQ-multi-protocol-18)". Rewrite the option 7 Bad bullet as: "Bad, because a proxy rewrites metadata and coordinator responses, and its Phases see record batches with no per-message Route or Consumer. Under P7 those records would reach Policies only as `onChunk`, where `authz.*`, `ratelimit` and `quota` do not run."

blocking.section: Decision outcome (MQTT embedded broker row); Decision outcome > Consequences; Decision outcome > Confirmation
blocking.issue: The embedded broker's core contract is still an unconfirmed spike in the owning document. That contract is: a QoS 1 PUBACK is sent only after the Upstream call settles, with up to ReceiveMaximum 16 (target) PUBLISHes in flight per connection. The research file lists mochi-mqtt's hooks but shows no way to defer a PUBACK asynchronously. Suppose the broker processes a client's packets in order and sends PUBACK when the publish hook returns. Then holding PUBACK for a Route timeout blocks that connection's reads, including PINGREQ and later PUBLISHes. ReceiveMaximum 16 then gives at most one in-flight PUBLISH, and the documented fallback, PUBACK on receipt, weakens acknowledgment to receipt by the Node, before any Upstream call. The ADR states neither this risk nor the fallback. It does not name the hook that turns a PUBLISH into a request. Its Confirmation checks only PUBACK codes. The chosen library may not support the design, and the ADR presents the ReceiveMaximum setting as a Good consequence.
blocking.evidence: ADR row: "| MQTT embedded broker | `github.com/mochi-mqtt/server/v2` v2.7.x, core and auth packages only | `OnConnectAuthenticate` and `OnACLCheck` hooks (CONNECT credentials: OQ-multi-protocol-7); no persistent sessions, ...". Consequences: "Good, because mochi-mqtt passes the Paho interoperability tests and exposes `MaximumPacketSize` and `ReceiveMaximum` ..., which the embedded broker sets to at most `maxRequestBodyBytes` and to 16 (target)." Confirmation: "and embedded broker PUBACK codes with a Paho client." Owning doc, Embedded MQTT broker mode: "| Acknowledgment | QoS 1 PUBACK after the Upstream call settles, reason code set in `onResponse`". OQ-multi-protocol-10: "Spikes: held PUBACK blocking reads (fallback: PUBACK on receipt)". Research section on mochi-mqtt lists hook events (`OnPublish`, `OnQosPublish`, ...) and capabilities, but says nothing about deferring acknowledgments.
blocking.fix: Add to Consequences: "- Bad, because no research shows that mochi-mqtt can hold a QoS 1 PUBACK until the Upstream call settles without blocking that connection's reads. If it cannot, `ReceiveMaximum` 16 (target) allows one in-flight PUBLISH per connection, and the OQ-multi-protocol-10 fallback, PUBACK on receipt, weakens acknowledgment to receipt by the Node." In the MQTT embedded broker row, add: "PUBLISH enters its Route from a publish hook such as `OnPublish`; PUBACK timing follows the OQ-multi-protocol-10 spike". Add a Confirmation bullet: "- **Held-PUBACK spike**, Planned (M4), before the embedded broker ships: one connection sends 16 QoS 1 PUBLISHes to a Route whose Upstream answers slowly. The test asserts 16 concurrent Upstream calls and a PINGRESP within the keep-alive. If it fails, the fallback applies and this ADR is amended."

blocking.issue: Every Node dials each `mqtt` Upstream through autopaho, but the ADR fixes neither the MQTT client identifier nor whether session and queue state persist. The research shows paho.golang offers session state persistence, a `Queue`, `CleanStartOnInitialConnection` and `SessionExpiryInterval`. The catalog cites 'session persistence' as a reason to select it. Suppose all Nodes present one client identifier derived from the Revision. An MQTT server disconnects the older connection when the same identifier connects again, so Nodes would take over each other's sessions in a reconnect loop across the Cluster. That is hidden coordination between Nodes, and it contradicts P4. This takeover rule comes from the MQTT specification, not from the research file, so a spike must confirm it. A persistent session or a file-backed queue would also keep durable state outside pack section 8.11 and leave orphaned broker sessions on scale-in.
blocking.evidence: ADR row: "| MQTT client | `github.com/eclipse/paho.golang` v0.23.x, `autopaho` | `mqtt` Upstreams; QoS 1 publishes await `PUBACK`; the consume mapping is undecided (OQ-multi-protocol-10) |". Research (go-libraries-protocols.md, paho.golang): "v0.20 introduced session state persistence and full QoS 1/2 support" and "autopaho `ClientConfig` fields include ... `CleanStartOnInitialConnection`, `SessionExpiryInterval` and `Queue`". Tech stack catalog: "MQTT v5, session persistence, QoS 1 and 2". Vision P4: "Nodes hold no durable state beyond their enrollment identity, Last-Known-Good configuration and disposable Plugin caches, and join or leave a Cluster without coordinating with other Nodes." Pack 8.11: "A Node persists only the following under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`".
blocking.fix: Add to the MQTT client row: "each Node connects with its own client identifier derived from `node.id` and the Upstream name, with `CleanStartOnInitialConnection` true, `SessionExpiryInterval` 0 and an in-memory `Queue`, so no session or queue state outlives the connection or the Node (P4, pack 8.11)". Extend the integration-test Confirmation bullet: "two Nodes publishing to one Mosquitto broker see no session-takeover disconnects". If the owning document must decide this first, add it under OQ-multi-protocol-8 as a proposed amendment in More information, and add a Bad consequence that the rule is pending.

blocking.section: Decision drivers (Acknowledged publishing); Decision outcome (Kafka row)
blocking.issue: The ADR's own driver requires the client to report buffer limits. The Kafka row never says what bounds the franz-go producer buffer, or how long a buffered record's bytes stay reserved. A value can be as large as `maxRequestBodyBytes` (10 MiB proposed), so a bound on the record count alone allows gigabytes. When a publish times out, the request returns 502 and releases its `maxBufferedBytes` reservation. franz-go may still hold the record and send it later. Producer memory then escapes the Node-wide budget during a slow-broker incident, which is exactly when the buffer fills. As written, the design has no bound on producer memory.
blocking.evidence: ADR driver: "- **Acknowledged publishing**: the Node answers 202 only after the broker acknowledges, so the client MUST report acknowledgment and buffer limits." Kafka row: "`messaging.key` is the record key; idempotent producer, acknowledgment from all in-sync replicas; `ProducerLinger(0)` on Routes that await it, ...; ingress uses consumer groups ..." (no buffer bound). Consequences: "non-blocking produce on a full franz-go buffer awaits the OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike". Owning doc, Kafka, NATS JetStream and MQTT: "| Limits | Publish: value within `maxRequestBodyBytes`, bounded producer buffer". Research: "`ManualFlushing` with `MaxBufferedRecords` is available for batching". Configuration model, Body buffering and limits: "Across requests, all of it is reserved from `maxBufferedBytes`, one budget per Node".
blocking.fix: Add to the Kafka row: "the producer buffer is bounded by `MaxBufferedRecords` (research). Each record keeps its `maxBufferedBytes` reservation until franz-go resolves its produce promise, even after a 502 timeout, so the Node budget bounds producer memory. A byte bound on the franz-go buffer is part of the OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike." Add to the integration-test Confirmation: "with the Kafka container paused, publishes end in 503 or 502 while the Node's reserved bytes stay within `maxBufferedBytes`".

non_blocking.suggestion: `ProducerLinger` is a franz-go client option, not a per-record or per-Route setting. Every publish Route awaits the acknowledgment, so 'on Routes that await it' either has no effect or implies one client per Route. The owning document says 'Nodes set `ProducerLinger(0)`'. Write: '`ProducerLinger(0)` on every producer client (one per `kafka` Upstream)'.

Committing after settle works badly with cooperative or KIP-848 revocation. A partition can hold a message through up to 5 attempts (target), or a paused head message retried every 60 s (target). If the revoke callback waits for settlement, it can outlast the group's rebalance timeout and the member is expelled. State that on revocation a Node abandons unsettled messages without committing them, so the new owner redelivers them at least once, and that it never blocks the revocation beyond the group timeout.

Consequences depends on 'only an import rule' to keep mochi-mqtt's Redis (go-redis v8), Badger and Pebble hooks out of `ruralzd`. That rule is only a proposed amendment in More information. Badger or Pebble would also persist broker state on the Node, against P4. Until the depguard rule exists, extend the review checklist item: 'or imports any mochi-mqtt package other than the core and auth packages'.

non_blocking.section: Pros and cons of the options (External MQTT brokers only)
non_blocking.suggestion: This option is also the mochi-mqtt watch-list fallback ('Separate broker via paho.golang'). Device ingress would then depend on the undecided MQTT consume mapping, where every Node gets each message without shared subscriptions (OQ-multi-protocol-10). Add that to the Bad bullet, so the fallback's cost is visible when the watch-list trigger fires.

The protocol matrix lets embedded MQTT and topic ingress reach `kafka`, `nats` and `mqtt` Upstreams, not only `http`. The figure shows only `ti -.-> up` (http Upstream). Label that node 'http, kafka, nats or mqtt Upstream', or say in the caption that only the http case is drawn.

Pack section 7 writes `eclipse-paho/paho.golang`, the repository, and the row writes the module path `github.com/eclipse/paho.golang`. Both are correct according to the research, but write them as the catalog does: 'repository `eclipse-paho/paho.golang`, module `github.com/eclipse/paho.golang`'.

By the verifier's rule the body is about 1,400 words, against a maximum of 1,500. The four fixes add about 150 words. Keep them compact. If the body goes over, shorten the first More information bullet first, because it repeats owning-document links the body already gives. Do not cut text that answers these findings.
